# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is the short companion to [*Quasi-stars under infall*](../index.html). That book records how the tools
were built and tested: a steady envelope model, a Julia port of the radiation-hydrodynamics code TITAN, and
continuum and non-LTE line transfer for its snapshots. This one keeps only what they predict for the spectrum of a quasi-star that is
being fed, and asks how it compares with the Little Red Dots seen by JWST.

**The object.** A quasi-star of $10^6\,M_\odot$ (black hole of $10^5\,M_\odot$ inside), radius
$R = 8.4\times10^{15}$ cm, effective temperature 7300 K and luminosity $1.4\times10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$
[@santarelli2026lrd; @begelman2026]. Gas falls onto it from $30R$ at $3\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, freely, and stops in a
radiative shock at the photosphere. TITAN follows the star and the infall through $4.5\times10^8$ s (run W30).

**What the spectrum shows, in one paragraph.** The star's own light keeps the infall ionized out to about $4R$ and
partly ionized out to $100R$. Its far ultraviolet does it through the Lyman lines, so the X-rays of the shock do not
matter. Hα comes out in strong, narrow emission (equivalent width −800 Å, FWHM 360 km s$^{-1}$), with a steep
Balmer decrement (5.1–5.3) and no dust anywhere. Hβ and the higher Balmer lines show deep redshifted absorption,
the infall seen against the star. The Paschen and Brackett lines are strong, Lyα is weak, and the Balmer jump is
0.74 dex. The shock's X-rays mostly do not escape: $L_{2-10\,\rm keV}/L \approx 2\times10^{-4}$. All of this is
**[computed]** with the stated assumptions (@sec-nlte).

**The book in five chapters.**

1. The full non-LTE calculation on the TITAN run (@sec-nlte).
2. What LTE would have said, and why it is wrong here (@sec-lte).
3. A simple model that reproduces the full calculation with no transfer. Most of it is closed form, and it shows
   which ingredients matter (@sec-sm).
4. The whole emission spectrum, line by line and band by band, and what produces each part (@sec-spec).
5. The Little Red Dots: what JWST spectra show, and where this model agrees and where it does not (@sec-lrd).

::: {.callout-note title="How to read the status of a statement"}
**[computed]**: output of the code in the repository, reproducible with the commands in @sec-exp.
**[tested]**: a computed result checked by a test or a deliberate variation.
**[estimate]**: an order-of-magnitude argument.
**[interpretation]**: our reading of the results, not separately derived.
**[observed]**: a measurement reported in the literature, with its reference.
:::
